chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakklin (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said regarding the hadith of the atheist who asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Do you say that He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing?' Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) replied: 'He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He is All-Hearing without a sense organ, and All-Seeing without a tool. Rather, He hears by His Own Self and sees by His Own Self. My statement that He hears by His Self does not mean that His Hearing is one entity and His Self is another entity. Rather, I intended to express myself using terminology suitable for when I was being questioned, and to make you understand since you were the questioner. Thus, I say: He hears with His Entire Essence, not that His Entire Essence is a part of Him. I intended to make you understand and to express Myself. My only recourse in this matter is to affirm that He is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing, All-Knowing, All-Aware, without any difference in His Essence and without any difference in His Meaning.'

key_terms.يَسْمَعُ بِنَفْسِهِ: He hears by His Own Self/Essence

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq explain that God hears and sees without physical organs?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that God’s attributes of Hearing and Seeing are intrinsic to His Essence, distinct from created physical organs, thereby affirming divine simplicity and avoiding *tashbih* (anthropomorphism). This explanation serves as a linguistic concession to human understanding, ensuring that attributing these faculties to God does not imply composition or parts within His indivisible Self. The narration underscores the Shia theological stance that God’s knowledge and power are identical with His Essence, free from any internal differentiation.
